project_description_verbatim: The BLM, in consultation with the Hopi Tribe, are in the process of repatriating Native American Graves Protection Repatriation Act (NAGPRA) human remains and cultural items removed from BLM lands. There is a relationship of shared group identity that can be reasonably traced between the present day Hopi Tribe and an identifiable earlier group, represented by the ancestral remains. The remains and cultural items were removed during various permitted archaeological excavations in Washington and Kane Counties in the 1960’s, 1970’s and 1980’s from known archaeological sites on public land. As part of the repatriation, a request from the Hopi Tribe has been made to rebury the NAGPRA remains and cultural items on public land in one location in Kane County, Utah. This reburial location is an area that is unlikely to be disturbed and is monitored by recreation staff frequently. Reburial of American Indian and Alaska Native human remains and cultural items are closely tied to repatriations of those remains and objects by the BLM under the terms of NAGPRA.
